𝐠2​(𝒒,ω)\displaystyle{\bf g}_{2}(\boldsymbol{q},\omega) =\displaystyle= [ωq​𝒒^−(𝟙−𝒒^​𝒒^)⋅𝒗e]​[ωq​𝒒^−(𝟙−𝒒^​𝒒^)⋅𝒗e]​g0​(𝒒,ω)\displaystyle\biggl[\frac{\omega}{q}\,\boldsymbol{\hat{q}}-(\mathbb{1}-\boldsymbol{\hat{q}}\boldsymbol{\hat{q}})\cdot\boldsymbol{v}_{\text{e}}\biggr]\biggl[\frac{\omega}{q}\,\boldsymbol{\hat{q}}-(\mathbb{1}-\boldsymbol{\hat{q}}\boldsymbol{\hat{q}})\cdot\boldsymbol{v}_{\text{e}}\biggr]\,g_{0}(\boldsymbol{q},\omega) (111)
+(𝟙−𝒒^𝒒^)π2​v02N0​q[v02e−v−2/v02−(v02−v−2+vesc2)e−vesc2/v02].\displaystyle+(\mathbb{1}-\boldsymbol{\hat{q}}\boldsymbol{\hat{q}})\,\frac{\pi^{2}v_{0}^{2}}{N_{0}q}\Bigl[v_{0}^{2}\,e^{-v_{-}^{2}/v_{0}^{2}}-(v_{0}^{2}-v_{-}^{2}+v_{\text{esc}}^{2})\,e^{-v_{\text{esc}}^{2}/v_{0}^{2}}\Bigr]\,.

The following relations between the velocity integrals often help simplify the calculation:

𝒒⋅𝒈1​(𝒒,ω)=ω​g0​(𝒒,ω),𝒒⋅𝐠2​(𝒒,ω)=𝐠2​(𝒒,ω)⋅𝒒=ω​𝒈1​(𝒒,ω).\boldsymbol{q}\cdot\boldsymbol{g}_{1}(\boldsymbol{q},\omega)=\omega\,g_{0}(\boldsymbol{q},\omega)\,,\qquad\boldsymbol{q}\cdot{\bf g}_{2}(\boldsymbol{q},\omega)={\bf g}_{2}(\boldsymbol{q},\omega)\cdot\boldsymbol{q}=\omega\,\boldsymbol{g}_{1}(\boldsymbol{q},\omega)\,. (112)

They follow from 𝒒⋅𝒗χ=ω𝒒\boldsymbol{q}\cdot\boldsymbol{v}_{\chi}=\omega_{\boldsymbol{q}}, and can be easily checked using the explicit expressions above.

Appendix D Estimation of Single Phonon Excitation Rate in YIG

In this appendix, we explain the analytic estimation that results in the dashed curve in Fig. 1. For the standard SD interaction considered in Sec. III.1, the single phonon excitation rate is

Γ⁡(𝒗)=4​gχ2​ge2mV4​1Ω​∫d3​q(2​π)3​∑ν 2​π​δ​(ων,𝒌−ω𝒒)​|𝑭S,ν(e)|2,\Gamma(\boldsymbol{v})=\frac{4g_{\chi}^{2}g_{e}^{2}}{m_{V}^{4}}\frac{1}{\Omega}\int\frac{d^{3}q}{(2\pi)^{3}}\sum_{\nu}\,2\pi\,\delta\bigl(\omega_{\nu,\boldsymbol{k}}-\omega_{\boldsymbol{q}}\bigr)\,\bigl|\boldsymbol{F}_{S,\nu}^{(e)}\bigr|^{2}\,, (113)

where

𝑭S,ν(e)​(𝒒)=∑j=Fe3+e−Wj​(𝒒)​ei​𝑮⋅𝒙j0​𝒒⋅ϵν,𝒌,j∗2​mj​ων,𝒌​⟨𝑺e⟩j.\boldsymbol{F}_{S,\nu}^{(e)}(\boldsymbol{q})=\sum_{j=\text{Fe}^{3+}}e^{-W_{j}(\boldsymbol{q})}e^{i\boldsymbol{G}\cdot\boldsymbol{x}_{j}^{0}}\,\frac{\boldsymbol{q}\cdot\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{\nu,\boldsymbol{k},j}^{*}}{\sqrt{2m_{j}\omega_{\nu,\boldsymbol{k}}}}\,\langle\boldsymbol{S}_{e}\rangle_{j}\,. (114)

See Eqs. (41), (45) and (39). For YIG, ν\nu runs from 1 to 240. However, since DM has same-sign couplings to all the Fe3+ ions (and zero couplings to the other ions), we expect acoustic phonons to give an 𝒪⁡(1)\mathcal{O}(1) contribution to the total rate at low momentum transfer. Further, the dot product 𝒒⋅ϵν,𝒌,j∗\boldsymbol{q}\cdot\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{\nu,\boldsymbol{k},j}^{*} in 𝑭S,ν(e)\boldsymbol{F}_{S,\nu}^{(e)} singles out the longitudinal acoustic branch, ν=3\nu=3, which has the following general properties at low momentum [100]:

ων=3,𝒌≃cs​k,ϵν=3,𝒌,j≃mjmcell​𝒌^,\omega_{\nu=3,\boldsymbol{k}}\simeq c_{s}k\,,\qquad\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{\nu=3,\boldsymbol{k},j}\simeq\sqrt{\frac{m_{j}}{m_{\text{cell}}}}\,\boldsymbol{\hat{k}}\,, (115)

where csc_{s} is the longitudinal acoustic sound speed. Also, we can set 𝑮=𝟎\boldsymbol{G}=\boldsymbol{0}, 𝒌=𝒒\boldsymbol{k}=\boldsymbol{q}, and Wj≃0W_{j}\simeq 0 at low qq. Therefore,

𝑭S,ν=3(e)​(𝒒)≃q2​mcell​cs​∑j=Fe3+⟨𝑺e⟩j=q2​mcell​cs​𝑺cell,\boldsymbol{F}_{S,\nu=3}^{(e)}(\boldsymbol{q})\simeq\sqrt{\frac{q}{2m_{\text{cell}}c_{s}}}\sum_{j=\text{Fe}^{3+}}\langle\boldsymbol{S}_{e}\rangle_{j}=\sqrt{\frac{q}{2m_{\text{cell}}c_{s}}}\,\boldsymbol{S}_{\text{cell}}\,, (116)

and the velocity-dependent rate becomes

Γ⁡(𝒗)\displaystyle\Gamma(\boldsymbol{v}) ≃\displaystyle\simeq gχ2​ge2mV4​2​Scell2Ω​mcell​cs​∫d3​q(2​π)2​δ​(cs​q−ω𝒒)​q\displaystyle\frac{g_{\chi}^{2}g_{e}^{2}}{m_{V}^{4}}\frac{2S_{\text{cell}}^{2}}{\Omega m_{\text{cell}}c_{s}}\int\frac{d^{3}q}{(2\pi)^{2}}\,\delta\bigl(c_{s}q-\omega_{\boldsymbol{q}}\bigr)\,q (117)
=\displaystyle= gχ2​ge2mV4​Scell2π​Ω​mcell​cs​∫d​q​q3​∫d​cos⁡θ​δ​(cs​q−q​v​cos⁡θ+q22​mχ)\displaystyle\frac{g_{\chi}^{2}g_{e}^{2}}{m_{V}^{4}}\frac{S_{\text{cell}}^{2}}{\pi\Omega m_{\text{cell}}c_{s}}\int dq\,q^{3}\int d\cos\theta\,\delta\biggl(c_{s}q-qv\cos\theta+\frac{q^{2}}{2m_{\chi}}\biggr)
=\displaystyle= gχ2​ge2mV4​Scell2π​Ω​mcell​cs​1v​∫d​q​q2​Θ​(v−vmin​(q)),\displaystyle\frac{g_{\chi}^{2}g_{e}^{2}}{m_{V}^{4}}\frac{S_{\text{cell}}^{2}}{\pi\Omega m_{\text{cell}}c_{s}}\frac{1}{v}\int dq\,q^{2}\,\Theta\bigl(v-v_{\text{min}}(q)\bigr)\,,

where

vmin​(q)≡q2​mχ+cs.v_{\text{min}}(q)\equiv\frac{q}{2m_{\chi}}+c_{s}\,. (118)

Now we can write the total rate per unit target mass in terms of the commonly used η\eta function, defined by

η⁡(vmin)≡∫d3​v​f⁡(𝒗)v​Θ​(v−vmin).\eta(v_{\text{min}})\equiv\int d^{3}v\frac{f(\boldsymbol{v})}{v}\,\Theta(v-v_{\text{min}})\,. (119)

The result is

R\displaystyle R ≃\displaystyle\simeq 1ρT​ρχmχ​gχ2​ge2mV4​Scell2π​Ω​mcell​cs​∫d​q​q2​η​(vmin​(q))\displaystyle\frac{1}{\rho_{T}}\frac{\rho_{\chi}}{m_{\chi}}\frac{g_{\chi}^{2}g_{e}^{2}}{m_{V}^{4}}\frac{S_{\text{cell}}^{2}}{\pi\Omega m_{\text{cell}}c_{s}}\int dq\,q^{2}\,\eta\bigl(v_{\text{min}}(q)\bigr) (120)
=\displaystyle= 1π​cs​(Scellmcell)2​gχ2​ge2mV4​ρχmχ​∫d​q​q2​η​(vmin​(q)).\displaystyle\frac{1}{\pi c_{s}}\biggl(\frac{S_{\text{cell}}}{m_{\text{cell}}}\biggr)^{2}\frac{g_{\chi}^{2}g_{e}^{2}}{m_{V}^{4}}\frac{\rho_{\chi}}{m_{\chi}}\int dq\,q^{2}\,\eta\bigl(v_{\text{min}}(q)\bigr)\,.

This is the formula we use to estimate the single phonon excitation rate in YIG in Sec. III.1. The material parameters are cs=7.2c_{s}=7.2 km/s [101], Scell=10S_{\text{cell}}=10, mcell=ρT​Ωm_{\text{cell}}=\rho_{T}\Omega, with ρT=4.95\rho_{T}=4.95 g/cm3, Ω=990.683\Omega=990.683 Å3. The analytic expression for the η⁡(vmin)\eta(v_{\text{min}}) function for the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of Eq. (101) can be found in e.g. Ref. [33]. Since the η\eta function has support up to qmax≃2​mχ​(ve+vesc)q_{\text{max}}\simeq 2m_{\chi}(v_{\text{e}}+v_{\text{esc}}), we cut off the dashed curve in Fig. 1 at the mχm_{\chi} value for which qmaxq_{\text{max}} reaches πΩ1/3\frac{\pi}{\Omega^{1/3}}, roughly the edge of the 1BZ.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.
